questions.subject: Lion
questions.explanation: This is a Lion, known as the 'King of the Jungle', though they live in savannas.
questions.articleBody: The lion is a large cat of the genus Panthera native to Africa and India. It has a muscular, deep-chested body, short, rounded head, round ears, and a hairy tuft at the end of its tail.

questions.subject: Blue Whale
questions.explanation: This is the Blue Whale, the largest animal known to have ever lived.
questions.articleBody: The blue whale is a marine mammal belonging to the baleen whale parvorder Mysticeti. It is the largest animal known to have ever lived.

questions.subject: Cheetah
questions.explanation: This is a Cheetah, the fastest land animal, distinguished by its tear marks.
questions.articleBody: The cheetah is a large cat native to Africa and central Iran. It is the fastest land animal, capable of running at 80 to 128 km/h.

questions.subject: Giraffe
questions.explanation: This is a Giraffe, the tallest living terrestrial animal.
questions.articleBody: The giraffe is a tall African hoofed mammal belonging to the genus Giraffa. It is the tallest living terrestrial animal and the largest ruminant.

questions.subject: Kangaroo
questions.explanation: This is a Kangaroo, a marsupial from Australia known for hopping.
questions.articleBody: Kangaroos are marsupials indigenous to Australia. They have large, powerful hind legs, large feet adapted for leaping, a long muscular tail for balance, and a small head.

questions.subject: Polar Bear
questions.explanation: This is a Polar Bear, native to the Arctic Circle.
questions.articleBody: The polar bear is a hypercarnivorous bear whose native range lies largely within the Arctic Circle. It is the largest extant bear species, as well as the largest extant land carnivore.

questions.subject: Octopus
questions.explanation: This is an Octopus, known for its eight limbs and high intelligence.
questions.articleBody: An octopus is a soft-bodied, eight-limbed mollusc of the order Octopoda. The order consists of some 300 species and is grouped within the class Cephalopoda.

questions.subject: Chameleon
questions.explanation: This is a Chameleon, famous for its ability to change color.
questions.articleBody: Chameleons are a distinctive and highly specialized clade of Old World lizards with 200 species described. They are noted for their ability to change skin coloration.

questions.subject: Sloth
questions.explanation: This is a Sloth, known for its slowness of movement.
questions.articleBody: Sloths are Neotropical xenarthran mammals. They are noted for their slowness of movement and extremely slow metabolism.

questions.subject: Platypus
questions.explanation: This is a Platypus, an egg-laying mammal with a duck-like bill.
questions.articleBody: The platypus is a semiaquatic, egg-laying mammal endemic to eastern Australia. It is one of the five extant species of monotremes, the only mammals that lay eggs instead of giving birth to live young.

questions.subject: Zebra
questions.explanation: This is a Zebra, known for its black and white stripes.
questions.articleBody: Zebras are African equines with distinctive black-and-white striped coats. There are three extant species: the Grévy's zebra, plains zebra, and the mountain zebra.

questions.subject: Rhinoceros
questions.explanation: This is a Rhinoceros, known for its horn(s).
questions.articleBody: A rhinoceros is any of the five extant species of odd-toed ungulates in the family Rhinocerotidae. Two of the extant species are native to Africa, and three to South and Southeast Asia.

questions.subject: Hippopotamus
questions.explanation: This is a Hippopotamus.
questions.articleBody: The hippopotamus, also called the hippo, is a large, mostly herbivorous, semiaquatic mammal and ungulate native to sub-Saharan Africa.

questions.subject: Gorilla
questions.explanation: This is a Gorilla, the largest living primate.
questions.articleBody: Gorillas are herbivorous, predominantly ground-dwelling great apes that inhabit the tropical forests of equatorial Africa.

questions.subject: Giant Panda
questions.explanation: This is a Giant Panda, native to China.
questions.articleBody: The giant panda is a bear species endemic to China. It is characterised by its bold black-and-white coat and rotund body.

questions.subject: Elephant
questions.explanation: This is an Elephant.
questions.articleBody: Elephants are the largest existing land animals. Three species are currently recognised: the African bush elephant, the African forest elephant, and the Asian elephant.

questions.subject: Sunflower
questions.explanation: This is a Sunflower, recognizable by its large yellow head.
questions.articleBody: Sunflowers possess a behavior called heliotropism. The flower buds and young blossoms will face east in the morning and follow the sun across the sky.

questions.subject: Venus Flytrap
questions.explanation: This is a Venus Flytrap, a carnivorous plant.
questions.articleBody: The Venus flytrap is a carnivorous plant native to subtropical wetlands on the East Coast of the United States. It catches its prey—chiefly insects and arachnids.

questions.subject: Bamboo
questions.explanation: This is Bamboo, the fastest growing plant in the world.
questions.articleBody: Bamboos are a diverse group of evergreen perennial flowering plants in the subfamily Bambusoideae of the grass family Poaceae.

questions.subject: Cactus
questions.questionText: What type of plant is this?
questions.explanation: This is a Cactus, adapted to hot, dry climates.
questions.articleBody: A cactus is a member of the plant family Cactaceae. Most cacti live in habitats subject to at least some drought. Many live in extremely dry environments.

questions.subject: Lotus Flower
questions.explanation: This is a Lotus flower, a symbol of purity.
questions.articleBody: Nelumbo nucifera, also known as the sacred lotus, is a species of aquatic plant. It is a sacred flower in both Hinduism and Buddhism.

questions.subject: Fern
questions.explanation: This is a Fern, a flowerless plant that reproduces via spores.
questions.articleBody: A fern is a member of a group of vascular plants that reproduce via spores and have neither seeds nor flowers. They differ from mosses by being vascular.

questions.subject: Moss
questions.explanation: This is Moss, a non-vascular plant commonly found in damp areas.
questions.articleBody: Mosses are small, non-vascular flowerless plants in the taxonomic division Bryophyta. They do not have true roots, stems, or leaves.

questions.subject: Oak Tree
questions.explanation: This is an Oak tree, known for its acorns and lobed leaves.
questions.articleBody: An oak is a tree or shrub in the genus Quercus. The fruit is a nut called an acorn, sitting in a cup-like structure known as a cupule.

questions.subject: Rose
questions.explanation: This is a Rose, a woody perennial flowering plant.
questions.articleBody: A rose is a woody perennial flowering plant of the genus Rosa, in the family Rosaceae, or the flower it bears. There are over three hundred species.

questions.subject: Lavender Field
questions.explanation: This is Lavender, known for its purple color and fragrance.
questions.articleBody: Lavandula (common name lavender) is a genus of 47 known species of flowering plants in the mint family, Lamiaceae.

questions.subject: Tulip
questions.explanation: This is a Tulip.
questions.articleBody: Tulips are a genus of spring-blooming perennial herbaceous bulbiferous geophytes. They are known for their bright colors.

questions.subject: Orchid
questions.explanation: This is an Orchid.
questions.articleBody: The Orchidaceae are a diverse and widespread family of flowering plants, with blooms that are often colourful and fragrant.

questions.subject: Daisy
questions.explanation: This is a Daisy.
questions.articleBody: Bellis perennis is a common European species of daisy, of the family Asteraceae, often considered the archetypal species of that name.

questions.subject: Dandelion
questions.explanation: This is a Dandelion.
questions.articleBody: Taraxacum is a large genus of flowering plants in the family Asteraceae, which consists of species commonly known as dandelions.

questions.subject: Union Jack Flag
questions.questionText: Which country does this flag belong to?
questions.explanation: This is the Union Jack, the flag of the United Kingdom.
questions.articleBody: The national flag of the United Kingdom is the Union Jack, also known as the Union Flag. The design of the Union Jack dates back to the Act of Union 1801.

image.alt: Union Jack Flag - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Flag of Japan
questions.explanation: This is the flag of Japan, featuring the rising sun.
questions.articleBody: The national flag of Japan is a rectangular white banner bearing a crimson-red circle at its center. This flag is officially called Nisshōki ('sun-mark flag').

image.alt: Flag of Japan - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Flag of Canada
questions.explanation: This is the flag of Canada, featuring a maple leaf.
questions.articleBody: The National Flag of Canada, often referred to as the Canadian Flag or the Maple Leaf, consists of a red field with a white square at its centre in the ratio of 1:2:1.

image.alt: Flag of Canada - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Flag of United States
questions.explanation: This is the flag of the United States, with 50 stars and 13 stripes.
questions.articleBody: The national flag of the United States of America consists of thirteen equal horizontal stripes of red alternating with white, with a blue rectangle in the canton bearing fifty small, white, five-pointed stars.

image.alt: Flag of United States - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Flag of Brazil
questions.questionText: Which country does this flag represent?
questions.explanation: This is the flag of Brazil, with its green field and yellow rhombus.
questions.articleBody: The national flag of Brazil is a blue disc depicting a starry sky spaned by a curved band inscribed with the national motto 'Ordem e Progresso', within a yellow rhombus, on a green field.

image.alt: Flag of Brazil - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Flag of France
questions.explanation: This is the French Tricolour (Blue, White, Red).
questions.articleBody: The national flag of France is a tricolour flag featuring three vertical bands coloured blue, white, and red. It is known to English speakers as the French Tricolour.

image.alt: Flag of France - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Flag of Switzerland
questions.explanation: This is the square flag of Switzerland.
questions.articleBody: The flag of Switzerland displays a white cross in the centre of a square red field. The white cross is known as the Swiss cross.

image.alt: Flag of Switzerland - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Flag of India
questions.explanation: This is the flag of India, with the Ashoka Chakra in the center.
questions.articleBody: The National Flag of India is a horizontal rectangular tricolour of India saffron, white and India green; with the Ashoka Chakra, a 24-spoke wheel, in navy blue at its centre.

image.alt: Flag of India - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Flag of Australia
questions.questionText: Which country does this flag belong to?
questions.explanation: This is the Australian flag, featuring the Southern Cross.
questions.articleBody: The flag of Australia is a defaced Blue Ensign: a blue field with the Union Jack in the canton, and a large white seven-pointed star known as the Commonwealth Star... and the Southern Cross constellation.

image.alt: Flag of Australia - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Flag of South Africa
questions.explanation: This is the colorful flag of South Africa.
questions.articleBody: The flag of South Africa was designed in March 1994 and adopted on 27 April 1994. It features a horizontal Y-shape in green, with red, white, blue, black and yellow sections.

image.alt: Flag of South Africa - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Flag of Germany
questions.explanation: This is the flag of Germany (Black, Red, Gold).
questions.articleBody: The flag of Germany is a tricolour consisting of three equal horizontal bands displaying the national colours of Germany: black, red, and gold.

image.alt: Flag of Germany - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Flag of Italy
questions.questionText: Which country does this flag represent?
questions.explanation: This is the flag of Italy (Green, White, Red).
questions.articleBody: The flag of Italy is a tricolour featuring three equally sized vertical pales of green, white and red, with the green at the hoist side.

image.alt: Flag of Italy - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Flag of Spain
questions.explanation: This is the flag of Spain.
questions.articleBody: The flag of Spain consists of three horizontal stripes: red, yellow and red, the yellow stripe being twice the size of each red stripe.

image.alt: Flag of Spain - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Flag of China
questions.explanation: This is the flag of China.
questions.articleBody: The national flag of the People's Republic of China, also known as the Five-starred Red Flag, features a red field with five golden stars.

image.alt: Flag of China - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Flag of Argentina
questions.explanation: This is the flag of Argentina.
questions.articleBody: The national flag of Argentina is a triband, composed of three equally wide horizontal bands coloured light blue and white. It features the Sun of May.

image.alt: Flag of Argentina - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Ostrich
questions.explanation: This is an Ostrich, the largest living bird.
questions.articleBody: Ostriches are large flightless birds native to Africa. They lay the largest eggs of any living land animal. With the ability to run at 70 km/h, they are the fastest birds on land.

questions.subject: Emperor Penguin
questions.questionText: What type of bird is this?
questions.explanation: This is an Emperor Penguin, endemic to Antarctica.
questions.articleBody: The emperor penguin is the tallest and heaviest of all living penguin species and is endemic to Antarctica.

questions.subject: Hummingbird
questions.explanation: This is a Hummingbird, known for hovering.
questions.articleBody: Hummingbirds are birds native to the Americas. They are known for their ability to hover in mid-air by rapidly flapping their wings.

questions.subject: Bald Eagle
questions.explanation: This is a Bald Eagle, the national bird of the USA.
questions.articleBody: The bald eagle is a bird of prey found in North America. It is the national bird and national animal of the United States of America.

questions.subject: Owl
questions.explanation: This is an Owl, characterized by its large eyes and flat face.
questions.articleBody: Owls are birds from the order Strigiformes. Most are solitary and nocturnal. They possess large, forward-facing eyes and ear-holes.

questions.subject: Peacock
questions.explanation: This is a Peacock, known for its iridescent tail feathers.
questions.articleBody: Peafowl include three species of birds in the genus Pavo. The male peacock is known for his extravagant eye-spotted tail covert feathers.

questions.subject: Flamingo
questions.explanation: This is a Flamingo, famous for its pink color.
questions.articleBody: Flamingos are a type of wading bird in the family Phoenicopteridae. The bright pink colour of their feathers comes from the beta-carotene pigments in the organisms they eat.

questions.subject: Toucan
questions.explanation: This is a Toucan, recognized by its large colorful bill.
questions.articleBody: Toucans are members of the Neotropical near passerine bird family Ramphastidae. They are brightly marked and have large, often colorful bills.

questions.subject: Kiwi Bird
questions.explanation: This is a Kiwi, native to New Zealand.
questions.articleBody: Kiwi are flightless birds native to New Zealand, in the genus Apteryx and family Apterygidae. Approximately the size of a domestic chicken.

questions.subject: Albatross
questions.explanation: This is an Albatross, known for its immense wingspan.
questions.articleBody: Albatrosses are large seabirds in the family Diomedeidae. They have the longest wingspans of any extant birds, reaching up to 3.7 meters.

questions.subject: Puffin
questions.explanation: This is a Puffin, distinguished by its colorful beak.
questions.articleBody: Puffins are any of three species of small alcids in the bird genus Fratercula. They are pelagic seabirds that feed primarily by diving in the water.

questions.subject: Macaw
questions.explanation: This is a Macaw, a large colorful parrot.
questions.articleBody: Macaws are a group of New World parrots that are long-tailed and often colorful.

questions.subject: Swan
questions.explanation: This is a Swan.
questions.articleBody: Swans are birds of the family Anatidae within the genus Cygnus. The swans' closest relatives include the geese and ducks.

questions.subject: Kingfisher
questions.explanation: This is a Kingfisher.
questions.articleBody: Kingfishers are a family, the Alcedinidae, of small to medium-sized, brightly colored birds in the order Coraciiformes.

questions.subject: Giant Sequoia
questions.explanation: This is a Giant Sequoia, the largest tree by volume.
questions.articleBody: Sequoiadendron giganteum (giant sequoia) is the sole living species in the genus Sequoiadendron. They are the most massive trees on Earth.

questions.subject: Baobab Tree
questions.explanation: This is a Baobab, native to Africa and known for its thick trunk.
questions.articleBody: Adansonia is a genus of deciduous trees known as baobabs. They are native to Madagascar, mainland Africa, and Australia. They have swollen trunks.

questions.subject: Cherry Blossom Tree
questions.explanation: This is a Cherry Blossom tree (Sakura).
questions.articleBody: A cherry blossom is a flower of many trees of genus Prunus. They are known as sakura in Japan.

image.alt: Cherry Blossom Tree - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Maple Tree
questions.explanation: This is a Maple tree, famous for its syrup and leaf shape.
questions.articleBody: Maple is a genus of trees and shrubs. They are easily distinguished by their palmate leaves and winged fruits.

questions.subject: Bonsai Tree
questions.explanation: This is a Bonsai, a miniature tree grown in a container.
questions.articleBody: Bonsai is a Japanese art form which utilizes cultivation techniques to produce, in containers, small trees that mimic the shape and scale of full size trees.

questions.subject: Birch Tree
questions.explanation: This is a Birch tree, recognized by its white peeling bark.
questions.articleBody: A birch is a thin-leaved deciduous hardwood tree of the genus Betula. They are typically small to medium-sized trees with papery, white bark.

questions.subject: Weeping Willow
questions.explanation: This is a Weeping Willow, with distinctive drooping branches.
questions.articleBody: Salix babylonica (Babylon willow or weeping willow) is a species of willow native to dry areas of northern China, but cultivated for millennia.

questions.subject: Pine Tree
questions.questionText: What type of tree is this?
questions.explanation: This is a Pine tree.
questions.articleBody: A pine is any conifer in the genus Pinus of the family Pinaceae. Pines are long-lived, typically resinous trees.

questions.subject: Banyan Tree
questions.explanation: This is a Banyan tree, known for its aerial roots.
questions.articleBody: A banyan is a fig that begins its life as an epiphyte. Its aerial roots develop into woody trunks.

questions.subject: Redwood Tree
questions.explanation: This is a Coast Redwood, the tallest tree species.
questions.articleBody: Sequoia sempervirens is the sole living species of the genus Sequoia in the cypress family Cupressaceae. Common names include coast redwood and California redwood.

questions.subject: Spruce Tree
questions.questionText: What type of tree is this?
questions.explanation: This is a Spruce tree.
questions.articleBody: A spruce is a tree of the genus Picea, a genus of about 35 species of coniferous evergreen trees in the family Pinaceae, found in the northern temperate and boreal (taiga) regions of the Earth.

questions.subject: Magnolia Tree
questions.explanation: This is a Magnolia tree.
questions.articleBody: Magnolia is a large genus of about 210 flowering plant species in the subfamily Magnolioideae of the family Magnoliaceae.

questions.subject: Honey Bee
questions.explanation: This is a Honey Bee, crucial for pollination.
questions.articleBody: A honey bee is a eusocial flying insect within the genus Apis of the bee clade, all native to Eurasia.

questions.subject: Monarch Butterfly
questions.explanation: This is a Monarch Butterfly, known for its migration.
questions.articleBody: The monarch butterfly is a milkweed butterfly in the family Nymphalidae. It is arguably the most iconic butterfly in North America.

questions.subject: Ant Insect
questions.explanation: This is an Ant.
questions.articleBody: Ants are eusocial insects of the family Formicidae. They live in organized colonies.

questions.subject: Praying Mantis
questions.explanation: This is a Praying Mantis.
questions.articleBody: Mantises are an order of insects. They are often called praying mantises because of their typical 'prayer-like' stance.

questions.subject: Ladybug
questions.explanation: This is a Ladybug (Ladybird).
questions.articleBody: Coccinellidae is a widespread family of small beetles. They are commonly known as ladybugs.

questions.subject: Dragonfly
questions.explanation: This is a Dragonfly.
questions.articleBody: A dragonfly is an insect belonging to the order Odonata. Adult dragonflies are characterized by large, multifaceted eyes and two pairs of strong, transparent wings.

questions.subject: Mosquito
questions.explanation: This is a Mosquito.
questions.articleBody: Mosquitoes are members of a group of almost 3,600 species of small flies. The females of most species consume blood.

questions.subject: Grasshopper
questions.explanation: This is a Grasshopper.
questions.articleBody: Grasshoppers are a group of insects belonging to the suborder Caelifera. They are plant-eaters.

questions.subject: Firefly
questions.explanation: This is a Firefly, or lightning bug.
questions.articleBody: The Lampyridae are a family of insects in the beetle order Coleoptera. They are soft-bodied beetles that are commonly called fireflies.

questions.subject: Scarab Beetle
questions.explanation: This is a Scarab Beetle, sacred in ancient Egypt.
questions.articleBody: Scarabaeus sacer is a species of dung beetle belonging to the family Scarabaeidae. The species was venerated in ancient Egypt.

questions.subject: Bumblebee
questions.explanation: This is a Bumblebee, larger and fuzzier than a honey bee.
questions.articleBody: A bumblebee is any of over 250 species in the genus Bombus. They are social insects that form colonies with a single queen.

questions.subject: Atlas Moth
questions.explanation: This is an Atlas Moth.
questions.articleBody: Attacus atlas, the Atlas moth, is a large saturniid moth found in the tropical and subtropical forests of Southeast Asia.

questions.subject: Wasp
questions.explanation: This is a Wasp.
questions.articleBody: A wasp is any insect of the narrow-waisted suborder Apocrita of the order Hymenoptera which is neither a bee nor an ant.

questions.subject: Cicada
questions.questionText: What insect makes a loud sound?
questions.explanation: This is a Cicada.
questions.articleBody: Cicadas are insects in the superfamily Cicadoidea. They are best known for the songs sung by most, but not all, male cicadas.

questions.subject: Butterfly
questions.explanation: This is a Butterfly.
questions.articleBody: Butterflies are insects in the macrolepidopteran clade Rhopalocera from the order Lepidoptera, which also includes moths.

questions.subject: Fly Agaric Mushroom
questions.explanation: This is the Fly Agaric, the classic red toadstool.
questions.articleBody: Amanita muscaria, commonly known as the fly agaric or fly amanita, is a basidiomycete of the genus Amanita. It is also a muscimol mushroom.

image.alt: Fly Agaric Mushroom - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Black Truffle
questions.explanation: This is a Truffle, a prized culinary delicacy.
questions.articleBody: A truffle is the fruiting body of a subterranean ascomycete fungus. Truffles are highly prized as food.

questions.subject: Oyster Mushroom
questions.explanation: This is an Oyster Mushroom.
questions.articleBody: Pleurotus ostreatus, the oyster mushroom, is a common edible mushroom. It was first cultivated in Germany.

questions.subject: Food Mold
questions.questionText: What is growing on this food?
questions.explanation: This is Mold (Penicillium).
questions.articleBody: A mold is a fungus that grows in the form of multicellular filaments called hyphae.

questions.subject: Shiitake Mushroom
questions.explanation: This is a Shiitake mushroom.
questions.articleBody: The shiitake is an edible mushroom native to East Asia, which is cultivated and consumed in many Asian countries.

questions.subject: Enoki Mushroom
questions.explanation: These are Enoki mushrooms, known for their long stems.
questions.articleBody: Enokitake is a mushroom well known for its role in Japanese cuisine. Cultivated forms have long, thin white stems.

questions.subject: Puffball Mushroom
questions.explanation: This is a Puffball mushroom.
questions.articleBody: A puffball is a member of any of several groups of fungi in the division Basidiomycota. The puffballs were previously treated as a taxonomic group.

questions.subject: Morel Mushroom
questions.explanation: This is a Morel mushroom, with a honeycomb cap.
questions.articleBody: Morchella, the true morels, is a genus of edible sac fungi closely related to anatomically simpler cup fungi.

questions.subject: Chantarelle Mushroom
questions.explanation: This is a Chantarelle mushroom.
questions.articleBody: Chanterelle is the common name of several species of fungi. They are typically orange, yellow or white, fleshy and funnel-shaped.

questions.subject: Lion's Mane Mushroom
questions.explanation: This is Lion's Mane mushroom.
questions.articleBody: Hericium erinaceus is an edible mushroom and medicinal mushroom in the tooth fungus group. It can be identified by its long spines.

image.alt: Lion's Mane Mushroom - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Porcini Mushroom
questions.explanation: This is a Porcini mushroom (Boletus edulis).
questions.articleBody: Boletus edulis, commonly known as penny bun or porcini, is a basidiomycete fungus, and the type species of the genus Boletus.

questions.subject: Death Cap
questions.questionText: Warning: What is this poisonous mushroom?
questions.explanation: This is the Death Cap, highly poisonous.
questions.articleBody: Amanita phalloides, commonly known as the death cap, is one of the most poisonous of all known mushrooms.

questions.subject: Turkey Tail
questions.explanation: This is Turkey Tail fungus.
questions.articleBody: Trametes versicolor – also known as Coriolus versicolor and Polyporus versicolor – is a common polypore mushroom found throughout the world.

questions.subject: Parthenon
questions.explanation: This is the Parthenon in Athens.
questions.articleBody: The Parthenon is a former temple on the Athenian Acropolis, Greece, dedicated to the goddess Athena.

questions.subject: Eiffel Tower
questions.explanation: This is the Eiffel Tower in Paris.
questions.articleBody: The Eiffel Tower is a wrought-iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris, France.

questions.subject: Taj Mahal
questions.explanation: This is the Taj Mahal in India.
questions.articleBody: The Taj Mahal is an ivory-white marble mausoleum on the right bank of the river Yamuna in Agra, India.

questions.subject: Colosseum
questions.explanation: This is the Colosseum in Rome.
questions.articleBody: The Colosseum is an oval amphitheatre in the centre of the city of Rome, Italy. It is the largest ancient amphitheatre ever built.

questions.subject: Great Wall of China
questions.explanation: This is the Great Wall of China.
questions.articleBody: The Great Wall of China is a series of fortifications that were built across the historical northern borders of ancient Chinese states.

image.alt: Great Wall of China - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Pyramids of Giza
questions.explanation: These are the Pyramids of Giza.
questions.articleBody: The Egyptian pyramids are ancient masonry structures located in Egypt. Most were built as tombs for the country's pharaohs.

image.alt: Pyramids of Giza - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Sydney Opera House
questions.explanation: This is the Sydney Opera House.
questions.articleBody: The Sydney Opera House is a multi-venue performing arts centre at Sydney Harbour in Sydney, Australia.

image.alt: Sydney Opera House - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Statue of Liberty
questions.explanation: This is the Statue of Liberty.
questions.articleBody: The Statue of Liberty is a colossal neoclassical sculpture on Liberty Island in New York Harbor within New York City.

image.alt: Statue of Liberty - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Burj Khalifa
questions.explanation: This is the Burj Khalifa, the world's tallest building.
questions.articleBody: The Burj Khalifa is a skyscraper in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. It has been the tallest structure and building in the world since 2009.

questions.subject: Machu Picchu
questions.explanation: This is Machu Picchu in Peru.
questions.articleBody: Machu Picchu is a 15th-century Inca citadel, located in the Eastern Cordillera of southern Peru.

questions.subject: Stonehenge
questions.explanation: This is Stonehenge in England.
questions.articleBody: Stonehenge is a prehistoric monument in Wiltshire, England. It consists of a ring of standing stones, each around 13 feet high.

questions.subject: Leaning Tower of Pisa
questions.explanation: This is the Leaning Tower of Pisa.
questions.articleBody: The Leaning Tower of Pisa is the campanile, or freestanding bell tower, of the cathedral of the Italian city of Pisa, known worldwide for its nearly four-degree lean.

image.alt: Leaning Tower of Pisa - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Golden Gate Bridge
questions.explanation: This is the Golden Gate Bridge in San Francisco.
questions.articleBody: The Golden Gate Bridge is a suspension bridge spanning the Golden Gate, the one-mile-wide strait connecting San Francisco Bay and the Pacific Ocean.

image.alt: Golden Gate Bridge - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Petra
questions.explanation: This is Al-Khazneh in Petra, Jordan.
questions.articleBody: Petra is a historical and archaeological city in southern Jordan. It is famous for its rock-cut architecture and water conduit system.

questions.subject: Light Bulb
questions.explanation: This is an incandescent Light Bulb.
questions.articleBody: An incandescent light bulb is an electric light with a wire filament heated until it glows.

questions.subject: Antique Telephone
questions.explanation: This is an early Telephone.
questions.articleBody: A telephone is a telecommunications device that permits two or more users to conduct a conversation when they are too far apart.

questions.subject: Wright Flyer Airplane
questions.explanation: This is the Wright Brothers' Airplane.
questions.articleBody: The Wright brothers were two American aviation pioneers generally credited with inventing, building, and flying the world's first successful motor-operated airplane.

image.alt: Wright Flyer Airplane - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Printing Press
questions.explanation: This is a Printing Press.
questions.articleBody: A printing press is a mechanical device for applying pressure to an inked surface resting upon a print medium (such as paper or cloth).

questions.subject: Wooden Wheel
questions.explanation: This is a Wheel.
questions.articleBody: The wheel is a circular component that is intended to rotate on an axle bearing.

questions.subject: Antique Compass
questions.explanation: This is a Compass.
questions.articleBody: A compass is a device that shows the cardinal directions used for navigation and geographic orientation.

questions.subject: Steam Engine
questions.explanation: This is a Steam Engine.
questions.articleBody: The Watt steam engine was an early steam engine and was one of the driving forces of the Industrial Revolution.

questions.subject: Antique Computer
questions.explanation: This is an early Computer.
questions.articleBody: A computer is a machine that can be instructed to carry out sequences of arithmetic or logical operations automatically via computer programming.

questions.subject: Antique Microscope
questions.explanation: This is a Microscope.
questions.articleBody: A microscope is a laboratory instrument used to examine objects that are too small to be seen by the naked eye.

questions.subject: Electronic Transistor
questions.explanation: This is a Transistor.
questions.articleBody: A transistor is a semiconductor device used to amplify or switch electrical signals and power.

questions.subject: Television
questions.explanation: This is an early Television set.
questions.articleBody: Television is a telecommunication medium used for transmitting moving images in monochrome (black and white), or in color, and in two or three dimensions and sound.

questions.subject: Camera
questions.explanation: This is a Camera.
questions.articleBody: A camera is an optical instrument to capture the visual image.

questions.subject: Model T Ford
questions.explanation: This is the Ford Model T.
questions.articleBody: The Ford Model T is an automobile that was produced by Ford Motor Company from October 1, 1908, to May 26, 1927.

image.alt: Model T Ford - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Microscope
questions.explanation: This is a Microscope.
questions.articleBody: A microscope is a laboratory instrument used to examine objects that are too small to be seen by the naked eye.

questions.subject: Mona Lisa
questions.explanation: This is the Mona Lisa by Leonardo da Vinci.
questions.articleBody: The Mona Lisa is a half-length portrait painting by Italian artist Leonardo da Vinci.

questions.subject: The Starry Night
questions.explanation: This is The Starry Night by Vincent van Gogh.
questions.articleBody: The Starry Night is an oil on canvas by the Dutch Post-Impressionist painter Vincent van Gogh.

image.alt: The Starry Night - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: The Scream Painting
questions.explanation: This is The Scream by Edvard Munch.
questions.articleBody: The Scream is the popular name given to a composition created by Norwegian Expressionist artist Edvard Munch in 1893.

image.alt: The Scream Painting - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: The Thinker Statue
questions.explanation: This is The Thinker by Auguste Rodin.
questions.articleBody: The Thinker is a bronze sculpture by Auguste Rodin, usually placed on a stone pedestal.

image.alt: The Thinker Statue - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: William Shakespeare Portrait
questions.explanation: This is William Shakespeare.
questions.articleBody: William Shakespeare was an English playwright, poet, and actor, widely regarded as the greatest writer in the English language.

image.alt: William Shakespeare Portrait - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Ludwig van Beethoven
questions.explanation: This is Ludwig van Beethoven.
questions.articleBody: Ludwig van Beethoven was a German composer and pianist. He remains one of the most admired composers in the history of Western music.

image.alt: Ludwig van Beethoven - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Origami Crane
questions.explanation: This is Origami, the art of paper folding.
questions.articleBody: Origami is the art of paper folding, which is often associated with Japanese culture.

questions.subject: Ballet Dancer
questions.explanation: This is Ballet.
questions.articleBody: Ballet is a type of performance dance that originated during the Italian Renaissance in the fifteenth century.

questions.subject: Romeo and Juliet Painting
questions.explanation: This depicts Romeo and Juliet.
questions.articleBody: Romeo and Juliet is a tragedy written by William Shakespeare about two young Italian star-crossed lovers.

image.alt: Romeo and Juliet Painting - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: The Great Wave off Kanagawa
questions.explanation: This is The Great Wave off Kanagawa by Hokusai.
questions.articleBody: The Great Wave off Kanagawa is a woodblock print by the Japanese ukiyo-e artist Hokusai.

image.alt: The Great Wave off Kanagawa - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Girl with a Pearl Earring
questions.explanation: This is Girl with a Pearl Earring by Vermeer.
questions.articleBody: Girl with a Pearl Earring is an oil painting by Dutch Golden Age painter Johannes Vermeer, dated c. 1665.

image.alt: Girl with a Pearl Earring - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: The Last Supper
questions.explanation: This is The Last Supper by Leonardo da Vinci.
questions.articleBody: The Last Supper is a late 15th-century mural painting by Italian artist Leonardo da Vinci housed by the refectory of the Convent of Santa Maria delle Grazie in Milan.

image.alt: The Last Supper - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: The Birth of Venus
questions.explanation: This is The Birth of Venus by Botticelli.
questions.articleBody: The Birth of Venus is a painting by the Italian artist Sandro Botticelli, probably made in the mid 1480s.

image.alt: The Birth of Venus - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: David Statue
questions.explanation: This is David by Michelangelo.
questions.articleBody: David is a masterpiece of Renaissance sculpture, created in marble between 1501 and 1504 by the Italian artist Michelangelo.

questions.subject: Mount Everest
questions.explanation: This is Mount Everest, the highest mountain on Earth.
questions.articleBody: Mount Everest is Earth's highest mountain above sea level, located in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range of the Himalayas.

questions.subject: Amazon River
questions.explanation: This is the Amazon River.
questions.articleBody: The Amazon River in South America is the largest river by discharge volume of water in the world.

questions.subject: Sahara Desert
questions.explanation: This is the Sahara Desert.
questions.articleBody: The Sahara is a desert on the African continent. It is the largest hot desert in the world.

questions.subject: Nile River
questions.explanation: This is the Nile River.
questions.articleBody: The Nile is a major north-flowing river in northeastern Africa. It is generally considered the longest river in the world.

questions.subject: Grand Canyon
questions.explanation: This is the Grand Canyon.
questions.articleBody: The Grand Canyon is a steep-sided canyon carved by the Colorado River in Arizona, United States.

questions.subject: Great Barrier Reef
questions.explanation: This is the Great Barrier Reef.
questions.articleBody: The Great Barrier Reef is the world's largest coral reef system composed of over 2,900 individual reefs and 900 islands.

image.alt: Great Barrier Reef - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Victoria Falls
questions.explanation: This is Victoria Falls.
questions.articleBody: Victoria Falls is a waterfall on the Zambezi River in southern Africa.

questions.subject: Dead Sea
questions.explanation: This is the Dead Sea, known for its high salt concentration allowing people to float.
questions.articleBody: The Dead Sea is a salt lake bordered by Jordan to the east and Israel and the West Bank to the west.

questions.subject: Antarctica Continent
questions.explanation: This is Antarctica.
questions.articleBody: Antarctica is Earth's southernmost continent. It contains the geographic South Pole.

questions.subject: Mount Fuji
questions.explanation: This is Mount Fuji, Japan's highest peak.
questions.articleBody: Mount Fuji is an active volcano about 100 kilometers southwest of Tokyo. It is the country's tallest peak.

questions.subject: Niagara Falls
questions.explanation: This is Niagara Falls.
questions.articleBody: Niagara Falls is a group of three waterfalls at the southern end of Niagara Gorge, spanning the border between the province of Ontario in Canada and the state of New York in the United States.

questions.subject: Mount Kilimanjaro
questions.explanation: This is Mount Kilimanjaro.
questions.articleBody: Mount Kilimanjaro is a dormant volcano in Tanzania. It is the highest mountain in Africa.

questions.subject: Yellowstone National Park
questions.explanation: This is Yellowstone (Grand Prismatic Spring).
questions.articleBody: Yellowstone National Park is an American national park located in the western United States. It is known for its wildlife and its many geothermal features.

image.alt: Yellowstone National Park - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Planet Saturn
questions.explanation: This is Saturn, famous for its ring system.
questions.articleBody: Saturn is the sixth planet from the Sun and the second-largest in the Solar System, after Jupiter. It is a gas giant with an average radius of about nine and a half times that of Earth.

questions.subject: The Moon
questions.explanation: This is Earth's Moon.
questions.articleBody: The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite. It is the fifth largest satellite in the Solar System and the largest and most massive relative to its parent planet.

questions.subject: Eagle Nebula
questions.explanation: This is the Eagle Nebula, specifically the Pillars of Creation.
questions.articleBody: The Eagle Nebula is a young open cluster of stars in the constellation Serpens. It contains the famous Pillars of Creation.

questions.subject: Mars Surface
questions.explanation: This is the surface of Mars, the Red Planet.
questions.articleBody: Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun and the second-smallest planet in the Solar System, being larger than only Mercury.

questions.subject: International Space Station
questions.explanation: This is the International Space Station (ISS).
questions.articleBody: The International Space Station (ISS) is a modular space station (habitable artificial satellite) in low Earth orbit.

image.alt: International Space Station - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Solar Eclipse
questions.explanation: This is a total Solar Eclipse.
questions.articleBody: A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon passes between the Earth and the Sun, thereby totally or partly obscuring the image of the Sun for a viewer on Earth.

questions.subject: Andromeda Galaxy
questions.explanation: This is the Andromeda Galaxy.
questions.articleBody: The Andromeda Galaxy is a barred spiral galaxy approximately 2.5 million light-years from Earth and the nearest major galaxy to the Milky Way.

questions.subject: Jupiter
questions.explanation: This is Jupiter, the largest planet in our solar system.
questions.articleBody: Jupiter is the fifth planet from the Sun and the largest in the Solar System. It is a gas giant with a mass one-thousandth that of the Sun, but two-and-a-half times that of all the other planets in the Solar System combined.

questions.subject: Space Shuttle
questions.explanation: This is the Space Shuttle Atlantis.
questions.articleBody: The Space Shuttle was a partially reusable low Earth orbital spacecraft system operated by the U.S. National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA).

questions.subject: Buzz Aldrin on Moon
questions.explanation: This is Buzz Aldrin during Apollo 11.
questions.articleBody: Apollo 11 was the spaceflight that first landed humans on the Moon. Commander Neil Armstrong and lunar module pilot Buzz Aldrin formed the American crew that landed the Apollo Lunar Module Eagle on July 20, 1969.

image.alt: Buzz Aldrin on Moon - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Black Hole
questions.explanation: This is a simulated image of a Black Hole.
questions.articleBody: A black hole is a region of spacetime where gravity is so strong that nothing—no particles or even electromagnetic radiation such as light—can escape from it.

questions.subject: Mars Rover
questions.explanation: This is the Curiosity Rover on Mars.
questions.articleBody: Curiosity is a car-sized Mars rover designed to explore the Gale crater on Mars as part of NASA's Mars Science Laboratory mission.

questions.subject: Full Moon
questions.explanation: This is the Moon.
questions.articleBody: The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite.

questions.subject: Planet Earth
questions.explanation: This is Planet Earth.
questions.articleBody: Earth is the third planet from the Sun and the only astronomical object known to harbor life.

questions.subject: Napoleon Bonaparte
questions.explanation: This is Emperor Napoleon Bonaparte.
questions.articleBody: Napoleon Bonaparte was a French military and political leader who rose to prominence during the French Revolution and led several successful campaigns during the Revolutionary Wars.

questions.subject: Tutankhamun Mask
questions.questionText: Which pharaoh does this mask belong to?
questions.explanation: This is the burial mask of Tutankhamun.
questions.articleBody: Tutankhamun was an ancient Egyptian pharaoh who was the last of his royal family to rule during the end of the 18th Dynasty.

questions.subject: Julius Caesar Bust
questions.explanation: This is a bust of Julius Caesar.
questions.articleBody: Gaius Julius Caesar was a Roman general and statesman who played a critical role in the events that led to the demise of the Roman Republic and the rise of the Roman Empire.

image.alt: Julius Caesar Bust - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Samurai Warrior
questions.questionText: What type of warrior is this?
questions.explanation: This is a Japanese Samurai.
questions.articleBody: Samurai were the hereditary military nobility and officer caste of medieval and early-modern Japan from the 12th century to their abolition in the 1870s.

questions.subject: Medieval Knight
questions.explanation: This is a medieval Knight in armor.
questions.articleBody: A knight is a person granted an honorary title of knighthood by a head of state (including the pope) or representative for service to the monarch, the church or the country.

questions.subject: Viking Ship
questions.questionText: Who used this type of ship?
questions.explanation: This is a Viking longship.
questions.articleBody: Vikings were the seafaring Norse people from southern Scandinavia (present-day Denmark, Norway and Sweden) who raided, pirated, traded and settled throughout parts of Europe.

questions.subject: Abraham Lincoln
questions.explanation: This is Abraham Lincoln.
questions.articleBody: Abraham Lincoln was an American lawyer and statesman who served as the 16th president of the United States from 1861 until his assassination in 1865.

questions.subject: Mahatma Gandhi
questions.explanation: This is Mahatma Gandhi.
questions.articleBody: Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi was an Indian lawyer, anti-colonial nationalist, and political ethicist, who employed nonviolent resistance to lead the successful campaign for India's independence from British rule.

questions.subject: Queen Elizabeth I
questions.explanation: This is Queen Elizabeth I of England.
questions.articleBody: Elizabeth I was Queen of England and Ireland from 17 November 1558 until her death in 1603. She was the last of the five monarchs of the House of Tudor.

image.alt: Queen Elizabeth I - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Rosetta Stone
questions.explanation: This is the Rosetta Stone, key to deciphering hieroglyphs.
questions.articleBody: The Rosetta Stone is a granodiorite stele inscribed with three versions of a decree issued in Memphis, Egypt, in 196 BC during the Ptolemaic dynasty.

questions.subject: Winston Churchill
questions.explanation: This is Winston Churchill.
questions.articleBody: Sir Winston Leonard Spencer Churchill was a British statesman, soldier, and writer who served as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom twice, notably during the Second World War.

questions.subject: Cleopatra
questions.explanation: This depicts Cleopatra VII.
questions.articleBody: Cleopatra VII Philopator was the last active ruler of the Ptolemaic Kingdom of Egypt.

questions.subject: Martin Luther King Jr.
questions.explanation: This is Martin Luther King Jr.
questions.articleBody: Martin Luther King Jr. was an American Baptist minister and activist who became the most visible spokesperson and leader in the civil rights movement.

image.alt: Martin Luther King Jr. - Wikimedia Commons image

questions.subject: Zeus / Jupiter
questions.explanation: This is Zeus (or Jupiter), King of the Gods.
questions.articleBody: Zeus is the sky and thunder god in ancient Greek religion, who rules as king of the gods of Mount Olympus.

questions.subject: Dragon
questions.explanation: This is a Dragon.
questions.articleBody: A dragon is a large, serpentine legendary creature that appears in the folklore of many cultures around the world.

questions.subject: Poseidon / Neptune
questions.explanation: This is Poseidon (Neptune), god of the sea.
questions.articleBody: Poseidon was one of the Twelve Olympians in ancient Greek religion and myth. He was god of the Sea, storms, earthquakes and horses.

questions.subject: Unicorn
questions.explanation: This is a Unicorn.
questions.articleBody: The unicorn is a legendary creature that has been described since antiquity as a beast with a single large, pointed, spiraling horn projecting from its forehead.

questions.subject: Sphinx
questions.explanation: This is the Great Sphinx.
questions.articleBody: The Great Sphinx of Giza is a limestone statue of a reclining sphinx, a mythical creature with the head of a human and the body of a lion.

questions.subject: Thor
questions.explanation: This is Thor, wielding Mjolnir.
questions.articleBody: In Germanic mythology, Thor is a hammer-wielding god associated with thunder, lightning, storms, oak trees, strength, the protection of mankind, and also hallowing and fertility.

questions.subject: Medusa
questions.explanation: This is Medusa, with snakes for hair.
questions.articleBody: In Greek mythology, Medusa also called Gorgo, was one of the three monstrous Gorgons, generally described as winged human females with living venomous snakes in place of hair.

questions.subject: Anubis
questions.explanation: This is Anubis, god of the dead.
questions.articleBody: Anubis is the Greek name of the god of death, mummification, embalming, the afterlife, cemeteries, tombs, and the Underworld, in ancient Egyptian religion.

questions.subject: Phoenix
questions.explanation: This is a Phoenix, rising from ashes.
questions.articleBody: The phoenix is an immortal bird associated with Greek mythology that cyclically regenerates or is otherwise born again.

questions.subject: Centaur
questions.explanation: This is a Centaur.
questions.articleBody: A centaur is a creature from Greek mythology with the upper body of a human and the lower body and legs of a horse.

questions.subject: Hercules
questions.explanation: This is Hercules (Heracles), known for his strength.
questions.articleBody: Hercules is a Roman hero and god. He was the Roman equivalent of the Greek divine hero Heracles, son of Jupiter and the mortal Alcmene.

questions.subject: Odin
questions.explanation: This is Odin, the Allfather.
questions.articleBody: In Germanic mythology, Odin is a widely revered god. In Norse mythology, he is associated with wisdom, healing, death, royalty, the gallows, knowledge, war, battle, victory, sorcery, poetry, frenzy, and the runic alphabet.

questions.subject: Sushi
questions.explanation: This is Sushi, a Japanese dish of vinegared rice.
questions.articleBody: Sushi is a traditional Japanese dish of prepared vinegared rice, usually with some sugar and salt, accompanying a variety of ingredients, such as seafood and vegetables.

questions.subject: Pizza Margherita
questions.questionText: What type of pizza is this?
questions.explanation: This is Pizza Margherita, with tomatoes, mozzarella, and basil.
questions.articleBody: Pizza Margherita is a typical Neapolitan pizza, made with San Marzano tomatoes, mozzarella cheese, fresh basil, salt, and extra-virgin olive oil.

questions.subject: Croissant
questions.explanation: This is a Croissant, a buttery flaky pastry.
questions.articleBody: A croissant is a buttery, flaky, viennoiserie pastry of Austrian origin, named for its historical crescent shape.

questions.subject: Tacos
questions.explanation: These are Tacos.
questions.articleBody: A taco is a traditional Mexican dish consisting of a small hand-sized corn or wheat tortilla topped with a filling.

questions.subject: Macarons
questions.explanation: These are French Macarons.
questions.articleBody: A macaron is a sweet meringue-based confection made with egg white, icing sugar, granulated sugar, almond meal, and food colouring.

questions.subject: Paella
questions.explanation: This is Paella, originating from Valencia.
questions.articleBody: Paella is a rice dish originally from the Valencian Community. It is regarded as one of the community's identifying symbols.

questions.subject: Burger
questions.explanation: This is a Hamburger.
questions.articleBody: A hamburger is a food, typically considered a sandwich, consisting of one or more cooked patties of ground meat, usually beef, placed inside a sliced bread roll or bun.

questions.subject: Dim Sum
questions.explanation: This is Dim Sum, a style of Chinese cuisine.
questions.articleBody: Dim sum is a large range of small Chinese dishes that are traditionally enjoyed in restaurants for brunch.

questions.subject: Ice Cream
questions.explanation: This is Ice Cream.
questions.articleBody: Ice cream is a sweetened frozen food typically eaten as a snack or dessert. It may be made from milk or cream and is flavoured with a sweetener.

questions.subject: Coffee Beans
questions.explanation: These are roasted Coffee Beans.
questions.articleBody: A coffee bean is a seed of the Coffea plant and the source for coffee. It is the pip inside the red or purple fruit often referred to as a cherry.

questions.subject: Ramen
questions.explanation: This is Ramen, a Japanese noodle soup.
questions.articleBody: Ramen is a Japanese noodle soup. It consists of Chinese-style wheat noodles served in a meat or fish-based broth, often flavored with soy sauce or miso.

questions.subject: Curry
questions.explanation: This is Curry.
questions.articleBody: Curry is a variety of dishes originating in the Indian subcontinent that use a complex combination of spices or herbs, usually including ground turmeric, cumin, coriander, ginger, and fresh or dried chilies.

questions.subject: Pizza
questions.explanation: This is a Pizza.
questions.articleBody: Pizza is a dish of Italian origin consisting of a usually round, flat base of leavened wheat-based dough topped with tomatoes, cheese, and often various other ingredients.

questions.subject: Violin
questions.explanation: This is a Violin.
questions.articleBody: The violin is a wooden chordophone (string instrument) in the violin family. It is the smallest and highest-pitched instrument in the family in regular use.

questions.subject: Grand Piano
questions.explanation: This is a Grand Piano.
questions.articleBody: The piano is an acoustic, stringed musical instrument invented in Italy by Bartolomeo Cristofori around the year 1700.

questions.subject: Electric Guitar
questions.explanation: This is an Electric Guitar (Fender Stratocaster style).
questions.articleBody: An electric guitar is a guitar that requires external amplification to be heard at typical performance volumes.

questions.subject: Drum Kit
questions.questionText: What is this set of instruments?
questions.explanation: This is a Drum Kit.
questions.articleBody: A drum kit is a collection of drums, cymbals, and other percussion instruments, which are set up on stands to be played by a single player.

questions.subject: Saxophone
questions.explanation: This is a Saxophone.
questions.articleBody: The saxophone is a woodwind instrument. Saxophones are usually made of brass and played with a single-reed mouthpiece similar to that of the clarinet.

questions.subject: Trumpet
questions.explanation: This is a Trumpet.
questions.articleBody: A trumpet is a brass instrument used in classical and jazz ensembles. The trumpet group ranges from the piccolo trumpet to the bass trumpet.

questions.subject: Harp
questions.explanation: This is a Harp.
questions.articleBody: The harp is a stringed musical instrument that has a number of individual strings running at an angle to its soundboard; the strings are plucked with the fingers.

questions.subject: Microphone
questions.explanation: This is a vocal Microphone.
questions.articleBody: A microphone is a transducer that converts sound into an electrical signal.

questions.subject: Vinyl Record
questions.explanation: This is a Vinyl Record.
questions.articleBody: A phonograph record is an analog sound storage medium in the form of a flat object with an inscribed, modulated spiral groove.

questions.subject: Accordion
questions.explanation: This is an Accordion.
questions.articleBody: Accordions are a family of box-shaped musical instruments of the bellows-driven free-reed aerophone type.

questions.subject: Flute
questions.explanation: This is a Flute.
questions.articleBody: The flute is a family of musical instruments in the woodwind group. Unlike woodwind instruments with reeds, a flute is an aerophone or reedless wind instrument.

questions.subject: Cello
questions.explanation: This is a Cello.
questions.articleBody: The cello is a bowed (and occasionally plucked) string instrument of the violin family. Its four strings are usually tuned in perfect fifths.

questions.subject: Guitar
questions.explanation: This is a Guitar.
questions.articleBody: The guitar is a fretted musical instrument that usually has six strings.

questions.subject: Soccer Ball
questions.explanation: This is a Soccer ball.
questions.articleBody: Association football, more commonly known as football or soccer, is a team sport played with a spherical ball between two teams of 11 players.

questions.subject: Basketball Hoop
questions.explanation: This is a Basketball hoop.
questions.articleBody: Basketball is a team sport in which two teams, most commonly of five players each, opposing one another on a rectangular court, compete with the primary objective of shooting a basketball through the defender's hoop.

questions.subject: Tennis Racket
questions.explanation: This is a Tennis racket.
questions.articleBody: Tennis is a racket sport that can be played individually against a single opponent or between two teams of two players each.

questions.subject: Baseball
questions.explanation: This is a Baseball.
questions.articleBody: Baseball is a bat-and-ball game played between two opposing teams who take turns batting and fielding.

questions.subject: Golf Club
questions.explanation: This is a Golf club.
questions.articleBody: Golf is a club-and-ball sport in which players use various clubs to hit balls into a series of holes on a course in as few strokes as possible.

questions.subject: Formula 1 Car
questions.explanation: This is a Formula 1 car.
questions.articleBody: Formula One is the highest class of international racing for open-wheel single-seater formula racing cars.

questions.subject: Boxing Gloves
questions.explanation: These are Boxing gloves.
questions.articleBody: Boxing is a combat sport in which two people, usually wearing protective gloves and other protective equipment such as hand wraps and mouthguards, throw punches at each other.

questions.subject: Chess Board
questions.explanation: This is a Chess board.
questions.articleBody: Chess is a board game played between two players. It is sometimes called Western chess or international chess to distinguish it from related games.

questions.subject: Ice Hockey
questions.explanation: This is Ice Hockey.
questions.articleBody: Ice hockey is a contact team sport played on ice, usually in a rink, in which two teams of skaters use their sticks to shoot a vulcanized rubber puck into their opponent's net.

questions.subject: Olympic Rings
questions.questionText: What event does this symbol represent?
questions.explanation: These are the Olympic Rings.
questions.articleBody: The Olympic Games are leading international sporting events featuring summer and winter sports competitions in which thousands of athletes from around the world participate.

questions.subject: American Football
questions.explanation: This is an American Football.
questions.articleBody: American football is a team sport played by two teams of eleven players on a rectangular field with goalposts at each end.

questions.subject: Cricket
questions.explanation: This is a Cricket bat and ball.
questions.articleBody: Cricket is a bat-and-ball game played between two teams of eleven players on a field at the centre of which is a 22-yard pitch with a wicket at each end.

questions.subject: DNA Helix
questions.explanation: This is the DNA double helix.
questions.articleBody: Deoxyribonucleic acid is a polymer composed of two polynucleotide chains that coil around each other to form a double helix.

questions.subject: Atom Model
questions.explanation: This is a stylized model of an Atom.
questions.articleBody: An atom is the smallest unit of ordinary matter that forms a chemical element. Every solid, liquid, gas, and plasma is composed of neutral or ionized atoms.

questions.subject: Human Brain
questions.explanation: This is the Human Brain.
questions.articleBody: The human brain is the central organ of the human nervous system, and with the spinal cord makes up the central nervous system.

questions.subject: Volcano Eruption
questions.explanation: This is a Volcanic Eruption.
questions.articleBody: A volcano is a rupture in the crust of a planetary-mass object, such as Earth, that allows hot lava, volcanic ash, and gases to escape from a magma chamber below the surface.

questions.subject: Telescope
questions.explanation: This is an astronomical Telescope.
questions.articleBody: A telescope is an optical instrument using lenses, curved mirrors, or a combination of both to observe distant objects.

questions.subject: Periodic Table
questions.explanation: This is the Periodic Table of Elements.
questions.articleBody: The periodic table is a tabular display of the chemical elements. It is widely used in chemistry, physics, and other sciences.

questions.subject: Skeleton
questions.explanation: This is the Human Skeletal System.
questions.articleBody: The human skeleton is the internal framework of the human body. It is composed of around 270 bones at birth – this total decreases to around 206 bones by adulthood.

questions.subject: Laboratory Flask
questions.explanation: This is an Erlenmeyer Flask.
questions.articleBody: An Erlenmeyer flask, also known as a conical flask, is a type of laboratory flask which features a flat bottom, a conical body, and a cylindrical neck.

questions.subject: Lightning
questions.explanation: This is Lightning.
questions.articleBody: Lightning is a naturally occurring electrostatic discharge during which two electrically charged regions in the atmosphere or ground temporarily equalize themselves.

questions.subject: Prism Light
questions.explanation: This shows Refraction (Dispersion) of light through a prism.
questions.articleBody: In optics, a prism is a transparent optical element with flat, polished surfaces that refract light. At least two of the flat surfaces must have an angle between them.

questions.subject: Magnet
questions.explanation: This is a Magnet.
questions.articleBody: A magnet is a material or object that produces a magnetic field. This magnetic field is invisible but is responsible for the most notable property of a magnet: a force that pulls on other ferromagnetic materials.

questions.subject: Robot
questions.explanation: This is a humanoid Robot.
questions.articleBody: A robot is a machine—especially one programmable by a computer—capable of carrying out a complex series of actions automatically.

questions.subject: Glass of Water
questions.explanation: This is Water.
questions.articleBody: Water is an inorganic, transparent, tasteless, odorless, and nearly colorless chemical substance.

image.alt: Glass of Water - Wikimedia Commons image
